claude_proposed_widenings.name: grant_spellcasting_focus
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The hat can be used as a Spellcasting Focus for Wizard spells while held. No existing atom models 'this item qualifies as a spellcasting focus for a given class.'
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: While holding the hat, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: attempt_unknown_spell
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The core mechanic lets the bearer pick any Wizard spell they don't know (class-list open selection, level-bounded, material-cost-bounded) and attempt to cast it. grant_spell_access requires a fixed spellId and cannot model open-ended class-list selection.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: you can try to cast a level 1+ spell you don't know. The spell must be on the Wizard spell list, it must be of a level you can cast, and it can't have Material components costing more than 1,000 GP.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: DcSource.spell_level_plus_base
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The ability check DC is '10 plus the spell's level' — a dynamic value driven by the player's chosen spell at cast time. No existing DcSource variant expresses a DC derived from a chosen spell's level. The fixed variant requires a literal DC; innate_dc derives from ability+PB, not spell level.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: make an Intelligence (Arcana) check (DC 10 plus the spell's level)

claude_proposed_widenings.name: spawned_creature without control
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Failure table entries 81-85 and 86-90 spawn creatures that are explicitly not under the caster's control and act independently. The existing SpawnedCreaturePayload always requires a CreatureControl block (commandCost, initiative, etc.). An uncontrolled spawn has no valid control spec.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: A creature appears in an unoccupied space as close to you as possible. The creature isn't under your control and acts as it normally would, and it disappears after 1 hour or when it drops to 0 Hit Points.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: open_plane_portal
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Failure table entry 91-95 opens a two-way environmental portal to another plane. This is distinct from transport_exile (which relocates a creature) — the portal is a persistent world-space object. Destination is GM-determined (dm_agenda component), but the portal-creation mechanic itself needs a new atom.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: A vertical, 10-foot-diameter, two-way portal to another plane of existence opens in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you and remains open until the end of your next turn. The GM determines where it leads.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: apply_condition with standalone timed duration
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Failure table entries apply conditions with explicit self-contained durations ('Poisoned for 1 hour', 'Petrified until the end of your next turn') that are not tied to a host spell's concentration or persist lifecycle. apply_condition carries no duration field; in an instantaneous activation there is no host lifecycle to derive duration from.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: you suffer a bout of 'magic sickness' and have the Poisoned condition for 1 hour ... You have the Petrified condition until the end of your next turn.
